questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: The question and exclamation marks
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish question from exclamation marks
questions.stem: Item 0001: A clerk's note shows a sentence ending mark; how to tell a question mark from an exclamation mark?

options.text: The question mark signals an inquiry, while the exclamation mark signals strong feeling or emphasis.
They are interchangeable in all legal notes.
The question mark signals strong feeling, while the exclamation signals inquiry.
Both marks are decorative and carry no meaning.

questions.explanation: A question mark signals an inquiry and an exclamation mark signals strong feeling or emphasis. They are not interchangeable, swapped, or decorative.

questions.stem: Item 0002: Explain how to choose among candidate characters from a typed reading in a clerk's note.

answer.exemplar: Choose the candidate whose meaning fits the sentence context, not merely the one that matches the typing or pronunciation alone.

questions.explanation: Context and meaning decide the choice. Relying only on typing or pronunciation risks selecting a wrong homophone.

options.text: All variant forms are always wrong and should be deleted.
The variant form that conflicts with the standard should be flagged as wrong in this context.
No form is wrong because standards are optional.
The main standard form is wrong because variants are preferred.

questions.explanation: The variant conflicting with the standard should be flagged in this context. Not all variants are wrong, standards are not optional, and variants are not preferred.
questions.hint: Flag the variant that conflicts with the standard.

options.text: Two entries mean the dictionary is broken and should be discarded.
Two entries are always identical, so no challenge exists.
Two entries for one headword can confuse which meaning or form applies, requiring context to decide.
Two entries are a printing error with no meaning.

questions.explanation: Dual entries can confuse which meaning or form applies, so context is needed. They are not identical, a broken dictionary, or a printing error.

The document is written in a foreign language.
options.misconception: treats regional standard as foreign language

options.text: The characters have completely different meanings in the other standard.
Stroke endings and component placement may differ, slowing recognition.

questions.explanation: Differing stroke endings and component placement slow recognition. The other standard is not a foreign language, meaning-changing, or illegible.

questions.topic: What counts as a single stroke

questions.stem: Item 0006: Define what counts as a single stroke in a clerk's file note.

answer.exemplar: A single stroke is one continuous pen movement from start to finish without lifting the pen, even if it changes direction.

questions.explanation: One continuous pen movement counts as one stroke, including direction changes. Lifting the pen starts a new stroke.

questions.stem: Item 0007: How should the hook be counted?

options.text: It is a separate stroke because it changes direction.
options.misconception: counts direction change as new stroke

options.text: It is part of the same stroke because the pen never lifts between them.
It is a separate stroke because it is short.
It is not a stroke at all and should be ignored.

questions.explanation: The hook is part of the same stroke because the pen never lifts. Direction change, short length, and ignoring it are wrong counting rules.
questions.hint: No pen lift means one stroke.

All sentences get a question mark by default.

questions.explanation: Inquiries get question marks and strong statements get exclamation marks. Defaulting to one mark or omitting marks is wrong.

The verb sense entry, because the sentence uses the word as a verb.

questions.explanation: One continuous pen movement is one stroke regardless of direction changes. Counting changes, splitting, or denying curves are wrong rules.

questions.explanation: Continuity without a pen lift makes the hook part of the same stroke. Treating direction change as a new stroke is the tempting error.
questions.hint: No pen lift means one stroke.
